evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We run a financial-literacy program for first-generation college students. Many avoid asking questions in workshops or one-on-one advising sessions because they feel judged or embarrassed discussing money: not knowing how credit scores work, or having to say they can't afford something classmates take for granted. Sessions start with a short welcome, then the content. Students can write on paper or a phone, privately. The program is free and most advisers were first-generation students themselves. We don't have research on what these students value, just advisers' impressions that family and being first in the family to attend matter a lot. Students attend about six sessions a semester. Can you write a values-affirmation exercise for the start of sessions?
evals.expected_output: A values-affirmation exercise in the output template, with the check of the setting filled in and the value list labeled unconfirmed.
assertions: The value list leaves out money or career success, and is labeled unconfirmed with a recommendation to confirm it with students.
The writing prompt has both parts: why the value matters, and a specific time it mattered.
Places the exercise before the financial content, in private, and introduces it without calling it a way to feel better or more confident.
Does not schedule the exercise at all six sessions.
Names the cost of college or family financial pressure as something the exercise does not fix, says trial results are mixed, and promises no effect size.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Can you write a values affirmation exercise for our participants?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks who the participants are and what they feel judged about, when that happens, and what the setting offers, and drafts nothing.
assertions: Asks who the people are and what they feel judged about.
Asks when the judgment is felt, or how the exercise could be given before it.
Asks what people gain once they engage, or whether a practical barrier keeps them away.
Drafts no value list or prompt.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We run a peer support group in Lusaka for women living with HIV. Many stop attending after the sessions where people are invited to talk about disclosure, because they feel ashamed, and some have mentioned that their church community treats the diagnosis as a moral failing. The group is free, meets in a private room at the clinic, and members say it is the one place they are not judged. We'd like a short values exercise at the start of those sessions to help them feel less judged. Group facilitators are peer counselors, not clinicians; some members do not read. Can you draft it?
evals.expected_output: The skill drafts the exercise for review, leaves faith off the value list, and tells the user to get clinical review and a referral path in place before any use.
assertions: Leaves faith or religion off the value list, or reframes it, and says this is because the stigma is partly moral or religious.
Labels the value list unconfirmed.
Tells the user to have a clinical psychologist or counselor review the exercise and to set up a referral path before use.
Names the church community's judgment as something the exercise does not change.
Gives a spoken version done in private, not shared aloud with the group.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Students aren't coming to our financial aid office because it's off the main hallway and everyone can see who walks in. Can you write a values affirmation exercise so they feel less embarrassed about being seen?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the barrier is the office's visible location, which an affirmation does not change, and points to the skill for choosing an intervention.
assertions: Says the barrier is exposure built into where the office is, not a feeling to be eased.
Says the exercise would not change the fact that students are seen walking in.
Names select-intervention-levers.
Does not produce a values-affirmation exercise.
